assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolites and related molecular sieves with controlled pore architecture and active sites underpins refining, petrochemistry and emissions control. Structure-directing agents, new framework types and mechanistic understanding of shape selectivity link atomic structure directly to function, with decades of industrial impact.
assessment.attribution: Corma (catalytic design and industrial zeolite catalysts), Davis (new framework types, large-pore materials, organic structure-directing agents) and Zones (SDA design, e.g. SSZ-series, and Chevron catalysis) form a coherent trio. Others such as Tsapatsis and Yu are strong but more recent or more synthetic-framework oriented. Earlier zeolite contributors outside the list are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Mature: the field is long established with many independently confirmed frameworks and large-scale commercial use; recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Zeolite synthesis has many contributors, so any three-person selection is partly arbitrary.
I may be biased toward this area given my own field; fair division between synthetic and catalytic contributions is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling made aryl amines accessible under mild conditions and is among the most widely used reactions in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis. The impact is clear, broad and lasting, and mechanistic work established the catalytic cycles.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general catalytic amination and the ligand classes that made it practical. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is the precedent but is less decisive; the list supports a fair two- or three-person configuration. Priority disputes between the two main groups may complicate allocation.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and independently confirmed; it is a staple reaction in industry. The 2010 prize on cross-coupling is related but did not cover C-N coupling, so timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize may make some members hesitant.
Whether Kosugi's contribution warrants inclusion is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Crystal structures of nitrogenase revealed the FeMo cofactor, including the central carbide, and the combined structural, spectroscopic and kinetic work has shaped the mechanistic picture of biological nitrogen fixation. As a structural chemist I value that the claims rest on determined structures.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the key structural work on the MoFe protein and FeMo cofactor; Einsle determined the high-resolution structure showing the interstitial carbon; Seefeldt (with Dean) built the mechanistic framework with Hoffman. Dean, Ribbe and Hoffman-style contributions complicate a three-person limit, so allocation is difficult.
assessment.maturity: The cofactor structure is well confirmed. The catalytic mechanism, including the E4 Janus state and substrate-binding site, is still debated, so mechanism recognition is less mature than structure.
uncertainties: Detailed mechanism of N2 reduction is not settled.
Credit is spread across a larger community than three names; some contributors may be omitted.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silicas (M41S, MCM-41, SBA-15) opened a new class of porous solids with tunable pore size beyond zeolites and inspired mesostructured materials broadly, with applications in catalysis, adsorption and templating of other materials.
assessment.attribution: Kresge and Beck (Mobil) made the original M41S discovery; Ryoo extended templating to carbons and ordered frameworks; Stucky introduced SBA-15 and biomimetic routes; Zhao and Inagaki made major related contributions. Credit is distributed across Mobil, Japanese and US/Chinese groups, and the Mobil team's collective credit is hard to apportion.
assessment.maturity: Mature with extensive independent confirmation and reproduction, though industrial adoption has been more modest than for zeolites.
uncertainties: Original claim versus earlier work (e.g. low-density silica reports) and Mobil team credit split are uncertain.
Practical impact is more academic than for zeolite catalysts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The nanocrystalline mesoporous TiO2 dye-sensitized solar cell introduced a molecular photovoltaic concept with a high-surface-area semiconductor architecture, and influenced later photovoltaics and photoelectrochemistry. The materials design links structure and function in an appealing way.
assessment.attribution: The 1991 O'Regan and Grätzel paper is the defining contribution, with Grätzel as the clear intellectual leader. Hagfeldt contributed key mechanistic and later device development and could substitute for O'Regan. A two-person prize looks defensible.
assessment.maturity: Mature scientifically with extensive confirmation, though commercial impact has been limited and perovskite cells have partly eclipsed the area, which could weaken or complicate the timing argument.
uncertainties: Limited commercial success compared with the scientific influence.
Grätzel's later perovskite work could be seen as part of a combined configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes are a large, growing family of 2D transition-metal carbides and nitrides with tunable chemistry and applications in energy storage, electromagnetic shielding and catalysis. The discovery of exfoliating MAX phases to 2D sheets created a genuinely new materials family.
assessment.attribution: Naguib, Barsoum and Gogotsi jointly published the original Ti3C2 report (Drexel); Gogotsi and Barsoum then led the field's development. The credited trio maps cleanly onto the origin of the field, which makes attribution relatively fair.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across many laboratories, but only about 15 years old and real-world applications are still emerging, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Structural characterization of surface terminations is still imperfect.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enabled structure determination from nano- and microcrystals and time-resolved studies of reactions, a clear enabling method that lets a community see what it could not before, in a spirit close to my own work on small crystals.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the method's conceptual and technical demonstration with Fromme, Hajdu and colleagues in 2011; Schlichting contributed key time-resolved applications and instrumentation. Hajdu is a pioneer but his role is difficult to weigh; it is a large collaborative effort, so allocation is delicate.
assessment.maturity: The method is confirmed at several facilities, but the strongest chemistry results (e.g. time-resolved mechanisms) are still developing and some interpretations rely on data from limited time windows.
uncertainties: Large team and facility-driven science complicates attribution.
Overlap with electron diffraction and cryo-EM approaches may reduce its relative priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: PROTACs and molecular glue degraders create a new pharmacological modality by recruiting E3 ligases to degrade target proteins; the cereblon mechanism for thalidomide analogues and clinical progress add to the importance.
assessment.attribution: Crews (PROTAC concept and first demonstrations), Ciulli (VHL-based design and structural work on ternary complexes) and Handa (cereblon identification as thalidomide target) are central; Deshaies, Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim are also important, and a three-person limit makes fair allocation difficult.
assessment.maturity: Scientifically well supported with several PROTACs in late-stage clinical trials, but approval and long-term therapeutic impact are not yet established, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC drug yet, so timing is uncertain.
Credit between concept originators, structural biologists and molecular glue discoverers is contested.
